Theorem
[Projection theorem]1. ch5:5.6\group chapter-5 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0093

↗ gt.def5.5.hilbert-space ↗ gt.def5.6.orthogonal If $\M $ is a closed subspace of a Hilbert space $\Hspace $, every $x\in \Hspace $ has a unique decomposition $x=y+z$ with $y\in \M $ and $z\in \M ^\perp $.
Proof

Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0093

\sketch The parallelogram identity shows that a minimizing sequence for $\dist (x,\M )$ is Cauchy, hence converges to some $y\in \M $. Minimality of $\| x-y\| $ under variations $y+t y'$ implies $(x-y,y')=0$ for all $y'\in \M $. Orthogonality also proves uniqueness.

□
